cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Obesity – the state of being extremely overweight in an unhealthy way.

p.em: Example: Obesity is a major public health problem worldwide.

cosy-blockquote.p: Hormone – a chemical substance produced in the body that controls organs.

p.em: Example: Insulin is a vital hormone that regulates sugar levels.

cosy-blockquote.p: Injection – an act of putting medicine into the body using a needle.

p.em: Example: The patient requires a daily injection of medicine.

cosy-blockquote.p: Appetite – a natural desire to eat food or consume nutrients.

p.em: Example: He had a very small appetite because he was feeling sick.

cosy-blockquote.p: Somatic – relating to the body, as distinct from the mind.

p.em: Example: The drug has positive somatic effects on weight reduction.

cosy-blockquote.p: Therapy – treatment intended to heal or relieve a medical condition.

p.em: Example: Hormone therapy is highly effective for weight loss.

cosy-blockquote.p: Reduce – to make smaller or less in amount, degree, or size.

p.em: Example: This drug helps reduce strong food cravings.

cosy-blockquote.p: Urge – a strong desire or impulse to do something.

p.em: Example: He felt a sudden urge to eat a sweet chocolate bar.

cosy-blockquote.p: Result – a consequence, effect, or outcome of something.

p.em: Example: The somatic result of the therapy was outstanding.

cosy-blockquote.p: Health – the state of being free from illness or injury.

p.em: Example: Maintaining a normal weight is essential for good health.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
According to the article, how does a weekly injection of GLP-1 hormone rewire appetite circuits in the brain?
★ How do you personally maintain a healthy balance in your diet and lifestyle?

What evidence is presented in the study proving that obesity is primarily an endocrine disease rather than a lack of willpower?
★ Do you believe that weight loss is primarily a matter of willpower or biological genetics?

Based on the research findings, how does the synthesized hormone suppress a patient's food cravings?
★ What is your reaction when you hear about 'miracle' weight-loss drugs in the media?

According to the paper, what causes a patient's natural appetite to drop significantly within hours of treatment?
★ How often do you think about body image and societal pressure in your daily life?

What data presented in the article indicates that positive somatic weight loss also improves cardiac health?
★ Have you ever tried a strict diet or fitness program? What was the hardest part?

According to researchers, how can a long-term peptide therapy permanently reset our metabolic setpoint?
★ Do you think doctors rely too much on prescribing medicine instead of lifestyle changes?

Based on the text, what physiological changes occur when we reduce the rate of stomach emptying?
★ How do you feel about the pharmaceutical industry making massive profits from weight loss?

What evidence in the paper supports the idea that the drug suppresses the urge to engage in addictive behaviors like drinking?
★ What is the healthiest meal you know how to cook? Do you enjoy preparing it?

How does the study evaluate the somatic result of the trial in terms of fat-to-muscle ratio?
★ Do you think processed foods should be taxed more heavily to encourage healthy eating?

To what extent does the article show that pharmaceutical interventions are mandatory for public health preservation?
★ What is your favorite form of physical exercise, and how does it make you feel?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
If future research continues to support this hypothesis, a simple weekly injection will be recognized as the global standard for treating chronic metabolic disorders.
★ Would you take a safe weight-loss pill even if you only wanted to lose a few pounds?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, clinical definitions of obesity will transition completely from moral failures to endocrine receptor issues.
★ Do you think obesity will be completely eradicated by medical science within 50 years?

Imagine future research proves that this synthesized hormone permanently protects our arteries, how would insurance companies change premium rates?
★ Should health insurance companies pay for weight-loss medications for everyone who wants them?

If future research proves this discovery beyond doubt, our natural appetite will be monitored by smart biosensors to prevent nutrient shortages.
★ Do you think weight-loss drugs will make people care less about healthy eating and exercise?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, the somatic side effects of long-term GLP-1 therapy will be completely neutralized using custom gene blocks.
★ How can society promote body positivity while still encouraging medical health?

Imagine future research shows that peptide therapy can cure other addictive impulses, how would addiction clinics change their methods?
★ Would you support a ban on advertising fast food to children on television and online?

If future research continues to support this hypothesis, weight-loss drugs will reduce the incidence of diabetes by ninety percent globally.
★ Do you think future school lunches will be scientifically customized to fit each child's metabolism?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, the physical urge to consume hyper-processed sugars will disappear from human biology.
★ What is the most important lesson about physical wellness you have learned?

Imagine future research proves that the metabolic result of these drugs is permanent, would gym memberships become obsolete?
★ Do you believe that fast-food companies are intentionally designing addictive food products?

If future research continues to support this hypothesis, public health campaigns will focus purely on distribution rather than calorie-counting instructions.
★ How has your own attitude toward diet and fitness changed over the last five years?
